title: Connecting the tensor-categorical formulation of anyon condensation with operator algebras and entropic order parameters
abstract: Anyon condensation that describes the transition between topological quantum field theories can be formulated in the language of tensor categories or that of operator algebras. We deploy the formalism of Doplicher-Haag-Roberts bimodules over quasi-local $\mathrm{C}^{*}$-algebras recently developed in [1] to investigate anyon condensation, which is associated with an extension of a certain operator algebra. The connection between notions in the two formulations is thereby made manifest in an intuitive, diagrammatic manner. An entropic order parameter, as the quantum information-theoretic measure characterising a condensation, is naturally defined, and we give a very simple proof of a bound on it.
summary: This theoretical paper unifies two advanced mathematical descriptions—tensor categories and operator algebras—to study anyon condensation in topological matter. It introduces an entropic order parameter, providing a rigorous bound on this measure that characterizes the transition into a condensed phase. The work is significant for its deep mathematical connection between quantum information theory and exotic phases of matter.
main_problem: The paper aims to connect two formalisms—tensor-categorical and operator algebraic—used to describe anyon condensation in topological quantum field theories.
main_result: It establishes a manifest connection between these two frameworks and provides a simple proof for an upper bound on the entropic order parameter characterizing the condensation transition.
method: The authors deploy Doplicher-Haag-Roberts bimodules over quasi-local C*-algebras to investigate anyon condensation, relating this structure to tensor categories via module functors.
model_or_system: The study focuses on anyon condensation, which describes phase transitions between $(2+1)$-dimensional topological orders or TQFTs. The analysis uses models like quantum doubles ($S_3$) and product theories (e.g., double Fibonacci/Ising).
key_observables: Entropic order parameter $S(\omega|\omega \circ E)$, which is a quantum information-theoretic measure of condensation.
important_parameters: The quantum dimension ($d_A$) of the condensable algebra $A$, and the topological state $\omega$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a topological (gapped) boundary, restricting the scope to cases where the underlying MTC has trivial Witt class.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the free A-module functor connecting bulk theory ($\mathcal{C}$) to an interface ($\mathcal{C}_A$). Figure 2 relates simple objects in $	ext{Irr}(\mathcal{C})$ to localizable bimodules over the boundary algebra $M$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first defining the tensor-categorical view (using module categories) and then mapping this structure onto the operator algebraic framework using DHR bimodules, culminating in the derivation of bounds on the entropic order parameter.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the use of entanglement measures like relative entropy to characterize phase transitions is directly relevant to understanding quantum criticality and topological phases in strongly correlated electron systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: (a) The free A-module functor FA : C →CA with FA(X) = X ⊗A determines what happens when an anyon X from topological order C is brought to the interface described by the module category CA. D, sitting on the other side of this interface, is the post-condensation topological order to be identified below. (b) As A is the invisible topological line (depicted as a dashed line here and simply omitted in the following) on the interface CA, composing FA with the multiplication µ : A ⊗A →A, one finds that the bulk line A can end topologically on this interface.

Figure 2: (a) For a strongly tensor generating object M ∈CL and a sufficiently large l, any a ∈Irr(C) arises in the decomposition of the internal end End(M⊗l). (b) Acting an operator O ∈EndCL(M⊗l) on an element in the bimodule labelled by a, which is represented as a junction operator joining the bulk line a with the boundary lines M⊗l, amounts to bringing O close to the junction and performing the OPE. The latter produces another junction operator attached to a.

Figure 3: The bulk line a ∈Irr(C) can end topologically on the interface CA, and M is a strongly tensor generating object in CL. (a) An operator sits at the junction joining a with the lines M⊗l on the boundary. eO, obtained when hitting this junction operator with the interface by collapsing the C layer, becomes an element in A upon taking the inductive limit. (b) The action of eO via OPE. Repeating the arguments we made above [c.f. figure 2(b)], one realises that every bulk line in the TQFT D labels a bimodule over A; in fact, D ∼= DHR(A).
